$$U_{\mathrm{source}}=2B-2C.$$
It holds for the union of mouths, and every tip counted there has the required saturated-to-sparse type swap. Consequently the loss of two boundary units for each merger is recovered in the exact count of the original physical no- $P$  deficit.This verdict uses the written arguments and the granted receiver and freezing dependencies. It does not use finite controls as premises.1. The enlarged contact condition survives normalizationThe normalization claim is valid, including the assertion that every mouth label remains unchanged.Every initial endpoint in a mouth belongs to a prescribed source or prescribed complete contact comb. All endpoints of each such component are frozen. Thus no matching edge of that component can be used in a promotion bundle: using it would promote one of its endpoints. Neither its endpoints nor its actual matching edges disappear.Original selected vertices remain selected. A blank vertex cannot become selected through these operations, because promotion selects an existing endpoint at that same vertex. Therefore the  $P/T/$ blank labeling of every mouth is fixed throughout normalization, even where several mouths overlap.The initial complete components also behave as required:Prescribed sources and combs remain connected and complete, because their endpoints persist and no new endpoints are added.Other components may shrink or split.Every resulting component remains within its initial component. Thin containment is preserved, and deleting endpoints cannot create an all- $P$  unit square.The granted nonpositive-receiver theorem therefore applies to every remaining final component. Complete contact combs retain their granted whole charge zero.In particular, the coalesced union and the comb-end flags used to define  $O$  and  $J$  are determined by the initial prescribed data and remain valid at the final representative. There is no normalization-dependent contact assumption being silently added.2. Perpendicular mouths remain excludedThe separator argument in Section 2 survives the enlarged contact condition.Normalize  $H$  as in the note. If a vertical mouth  $F_K$  meets its horizontal mouth, their intersection contains a physical tile. Hence the vertical mouth’s two-column band lies between the arms of  $H$ , and it contains both rows  $r,r+1$ . Its tip rows consequently satisfy
$$u\le r-1,\qquad v\ge r+2.$$
The initial cases are correct:If  $u\le0$ , the vertex  $(1,c)$  belongs to the chamber of  $H$  and lies in  $F_K$ . It violates the contact condition for  $K$ .If  $u=1$ , the upper tip of  $K$  is already a vertex of  $H$ , contradicting distinct complete components.Otherwise the upper tip lies in
$$I=\{2,\ldots,r-1\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\},$$
and the lower tip lies outside it. A nearest-neighbor endpoint path in  $K$  must have a first exit from  $I$ . Its outside vertex lies in
$$\bigl(\{1,r\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\}\bigr)
\;\cup\;
\bigl(\{2,\ldots,r-1\}\times\{0,w-1\}\bigr).$$
The top and lateral parts belong to  $H$ , so exiting there joins the two endpoint components. The bottom part lies in  $F_H$ . A path in  $K$  exiting there places an endpoint of the perpendicular source  $K$  in  $F_H$ , which the enlarged contact condition still forbids.The crucial distinction is the identity of the path’s component: allowing comb endpoints and parallel-source tips on the bottom boundary does not make any of them usable by a path in  $K$ . All possible exits are excluded.Thus perpendicular mouths have no common physical tile. Because coalescing adds no tiles to their union, perpendicular coalesced strips also remain disjoint.3. Coalescing gives exactly  $2B-2C$  internal source tipsThis count is exact, including the treatment of tips that might otherwise be counted through another strip.The interval unionFor a group of mouths in one physical band, write
$$F_H=\{L_H+1,\ldots,R_H-1\}.$$
Merging overlapping or adjacent integer intervals produces their connected union. If
$$L=\min_H L_H,\qquad R=\max_H R_H,$$
that union is precisely
$$G_i=\{L+1,\ldots,R-1\}.$$
There is no added gap tile. Its  $2b_i$  source-tip tiles are distinct. $$2b_i-2$$
of these source-tip tiles therefore lie in  $G_i$ .This remains true for sources opening in opposite directions. The local identity and global signs are correctLet  $G_i$  contain  $n_i$  physical tiles and put

The physical type table gives

=2n_i-\mu_i+\frac{U_i-S_i}{2}.$$
Removing the two blank extreme vertex columns leaves  $n_i-1$  shifted squares counting exactly the same  $\mu_i$ . Since the singleton types swap, their corresponding formula is
$$D'_i
=2(n_i-1)-\mu_i+\frac{S_i-U_i}{2}.$$
Subtracting yields
$$D_i-D'_i
=2+U_i-S_i,$$
and hence
$$\boxed{D_i=2-S_i+U_i+D'_i.}$$
Every shifted no- $P$  square contains at most two selected vertices, so  $D'_i\ge0$ . $$S_{\mathrm{comb}}=I+O,\qquad
U_{\mathrm{comb}}=I+J.$$
All other singleton columns are saturated source tips. Therefore
$$\sum_i S_i=I+O,
\qquad
\sum_i U_i=I+J+2B-2C.$$

D_{\mathrm{total}}
&=2C-(I+O)+(I+J+2B-2C)+\sum_iD'_i\\
&=\boxed{2B+J-O+\sum_iD'_i}.
\end{aligned}$$
